utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would the registrar call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-98-32/1, the Prosecutor versus Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Who appears for the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Mark Harmon. Appearing with me, Mr. Frederic Ossogo, to my right. To my left, the case manager, Lise-Lotte Karlsson. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon. For the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, Your Honour. Chrissa Loukas. I appear for the accused as duty counsel assigned today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Loukas. Now, Mr. Lukic, could you stand, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you able at the moment to follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're hearing a clear translation?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you then confirm to me your full name.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker speak into the microphone, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 5th of April, 1961.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Place of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The village of Rujiste, Visegrad municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And the address at which you were resident immediately before you were transferred to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Seganje BB, no number, Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you currently employed?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Loukas, this is a rather ancient indictment which comes before the Court today. Has your client had an opportunity to read the indictment in a language which he clearly understands?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I've discussed this matter with Mr. Lukic, and I can indicate that he waives the reading of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now there are a total, I think, of 12 charges or 12 counts which involve him. In these circumstances, I assume it is sufficient if the Court Deputy simply summarises each individual count and takes a plea on each individual count from him.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. I can indicate, Your Honour, I foreshadowed to Mr. Lukic that that might be the procedure that's adopted and, Your Honour, there is no objection to that course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: For example, Count 1 would simply be stated as Count 1, extermination, a crime against humanity, and he would then be asked does he plead guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, yes. And he's aware of the procedure and is happy to proceed with that procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Lukic, would you stand again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The Court Deputy is now going to read to you each one of the 10 charges against you, but simply referring to the short description of the charge that I've just given an example of. And each time when she has read the summary of the count or charge, she will ask you whether you plead guilty or not guilty and you should say to her either "guilty" or "not guilty." Do you understand that? I'm sorry, I can't hear.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Court Deputy, could you follow that procedure, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 1, extermination, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 2, persecutions on political, racial, and religious grounds, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 10, murder, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 11, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 12, inhumane acts, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 13, violence to life and person, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 14, murder, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 15, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 16, inhumane acts, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 17, violation to life and person, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 18, inhumane acts, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 19, cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. In light of the pleas which have been tendered, the registry is ordered by me to note that a trial diet should be fixed in due course to deal with the case subject to any other proceedings which take place between now and then. You may now sit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Harmon, we have from you a motion to suspend all non-essential proceedings, a title which I found amusing in itself. I take it all proceedings that ever take place here are essential.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, it's not entirely clear to me what you mean by this, because there are certain things that have to take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, what we mean by this is that there is already on file in this case a motion to have this case referred to Bosnia. We are prepared to proceed in those proceedings. The request is to suspend litigation relating to a trial in this case. I say that, however, with the understanding that when permanent counsel is assigned within 30 days we will comply with our discovery obligations. But we wish to avoid extensive litigation prior to the filing up the proceedings that will occur under Rule 11 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The -- you rightly note that disclosure has to take place, I think. But disclosure itself will then have the trigger effect of starting the period for preliminary motions, at least two of which, or two categories of which, it seems to me, you could hardly suspend. I'm just concerned that a motion formulated in such broad and fairly vague terms at this stage is likely to lead to some misunderstanding, especially since nothing other than disclosure plus preliminary motions is likely to happen in the immediately foreseeable future. So my inclination is simply to note that the motion is there and not to make a determination of it just at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's satisfactory, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. But -- now, that's subject, obviously, to any comment you have to make on that motion, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I, of course, echo with Your Honour's sentiments in relation to the question of vagueness. The other point I'd like to make is this, as duty counsel, and that is the accused, Mr. Lukic, has sought the assignment of permanent counsel, and as I understand it that permanent counsel is - and I should note this for the record, for Your Honour as well - a Mr. Bezbradica who, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. as I understand it, is on the Rule 45 list of counsel and should hopefully be assigned in the not-too-distant future. And any questions in relation to motion or motions of this nature of course should await the assignment of permanent counsel. As duty counsel, of course, I certainly won't be accepting disclosure of the relevant material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Well, Mr. Lukic, could you stand again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It is very important - I cannot stress how important - that every effort is made to have your permanent counsel assigned at the earliest possible date. Because if there's any hold up or confusion in that arrangement, then in light of what's just been said you will end up with the papers in the case being delivered to you, and that is not a desirable situation to be in. If you intend to conduct the case through counsel, then it is vital that he gets the papers -- or he or she gets the papers delivered from the Prosecution as soon as possible. Now, have you already had discussions with Mr. Bezbradica?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have not talked to him yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So what is the plan you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I intend to have him come here to visit me. I have given him the telephone number, or rather, I gave him the telephone number once I arrived in the Detention Unit. I think the registry was provided with the telephone number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it is important that you yourself take action to make sure that the person you want does make arrangements to contact you, because you must find out quickly in case he's unable to take the case or finds difficulty with it, because you then will have to make alternative arrangements. And there is always the possibility that the 30 days that the Prosecution have for delivering the material to you will run out before you've made that arrangement. It is a very urgent matter. Now, do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, within a 30-day deadline Bezbradica should come here. Is that how I am to understand it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No. The maximum period that should elapse before all the material which the Prosecution have to disclose to you to backup their indictment, the maximum period they have is 30 days. So you must have your counsel in place before 30 days expires. You need to make immediate contact with a person who is able to represent you. Now, do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And the reason it's important is that when the material is handed over, the period then starts running for you to make what are called preliminary motions. That's certain motions which are defined in the Rules, and you only have 30 days in which to make these motions. Yes, 30 days from the date on which the material is disclosed to you. So, for example, if you were wanting to say that you shouldn't be here because the Tribunal has no jurisdiction, or if you were claiming that there's something in the indictment that's wrong that you are challenging, then you only have a short period of 30 days from getting the Prosecution material to make these legal challenges. So you need to have your legal advice in place, the person who is going to represent you, in place as soon as possible. You understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, is there any matter which you wish to raise directly with me?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the moment, nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sit down then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, are you aware of anything else that ought to be raised at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I've consulted with Mr. Lukic in relation to the various matters that one does consult with the accused on occasions of this nature, and there is nothing that I need to bring before the Court at this stage. I, of course, as Your Honour has done, emphasised to him the importance of ensuring that permanent counsel is assigned in view of the limited time period available under the Rules. And as I understand it -- and I, of course, will assist in the process of ensuring that contact is made with permanent counsel and also under the auspices of the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Harmon, anything else that requires to be dealt with at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, nothing, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. That completes the Initial Appearance and the court is now adjourned.
